commands.name: Add Track

commands.name: Pitch-Shift Clip

commands.name: Add Clip Effect
commands.args: { track, clip, type:"filter"|"step_volume"|"invert"|"make_mono"|"tape_stop", freq_hz? (filter only), highpass?:bool (filter only) }

commands.args: { track, clip, pitch, start_beat, length_beats, velocity? }

commands.name: Set MIDI Velocity
commands.args: { track, clip, value?:1-127, scale?:0..8, add?:-127..127, humanize?:0..1 (deterministic jitter, +/-32 at 1 - ONE call varies every note in the clip, so 'make them breathe' is one humanize call, not a per-note sweep), pitch?:0-127 (only that note), start_beat?, end_beat?, seed?:int }

commands.name: Set Clip Groove
commands.args: { track, clip, template?:<name from groove.list>|"" to remove, strength?:0..1 (Live's Amount) } - works on MIDI *and* AUDIO clips, NON-DESTRUCTIVELY. MIDI: notes keep their raw start_beat and the engine shifts them at playback (the snapshot's play_beat is a READOUT of where each note sounds - never write it back). AUDIO: the groove rides the clip's warp map, so the clip must have Warp on; hand-editing a warp marker detaches the groove

commands.name: Create Groove
commands.args: { name, notes_per_beat:1-8, latenesses:[-1..1 per grid cell, + = late / - = early], parameterized?:bool=true } - the shift is HALF the value x the cell, so ~0.66 on 1/8 cells is a triplet swing

commands.name: Tune Notes
commands.args: { track, clip, strength?:0..1=1 (how much of each error to remove), min_cents?:>=5=15 (leave smaller deviations alone) } - fix the OFF NOTES of a monophonic audio clip in place: the brain names every note beyond min_cents, then the clip is split at those note boundaries, each segment pitched by its own error, seams faded - ONE undo. Refuses polyphony (chords have no single pitch to correct), warped/reversed/grooved clips, and takes with more than 48 off notes (that is a re-take). Answers a moment later (async, like Extract Groove)

commands.name: Extract Groove
commands.args: { track, clip, name?, apply?:bool=true } - measure THIS clip's feel into a pool template. MIDI is immediate; an AUDIO clip is analysed by the brain and lands a moment later. Refuses with a reason when the part is quantized (nothing to take) or too dense for a straight grid

commands.name: Export Groove
commands.args: { name, path? (default: the Zammoth Grooves folder) } -> { file }

commands.name: Import Groove
commands.args: { path: a .trkgroove file OR a folder of them } -> { names:[...] }

commands.name: Groove Amount
commands.args: { amount: 0..1 } - scales EVERY grooved clip at once, on top of each clip's own strength (1 = each clip as set)

commands.name: Set Instrument
commands.args: { track, instrument: "synth"|"drums"|"sampler", kit?: "gm"|"empty"=empty (drums only: seed the GM kit, or blank pads) } - MIDI tracks only (track_kind "midi"); an audio track refuses

commands.name: Add Drum Kit
commands.args: { name?, kit?: "gm"|"empty"=gm } - gm = the 14-piece synthesised GM kit on the pads (a composed beat sounds); empty = a blank 16-pad kit like the user's browser Drum Kit

commands.name: Load Sample
commands.args: { track, path, note, name? } - refuses an occupied note (use sampler.replace_sound to swap)

commands.args: { track, index|note, gain_db?, pan?, open_ended?:bool, choke?:0-16 (0=off; same group = one cuts the other, hats ship in 1), tune?:semitones -48..48 }

commands.args: { track? } - kit becomes per-pad chains (KeyFilter->Simpler->FX); idempotent, one undo

commands.args: { track?, note, device: <native type e.g. comp|eq|saturation> OR name: <scanned plugin name> } - auto-promotes, then adds the device to that ONE pad's chain (one undo step)

commands.name: Set Synth Modulation
commands.args: { track, source, target, depth?:-1..1=0.5, clear?:bool } - one ROUTE of a WOOLLY (4OSC) synth's mod matrix (the track's mod_matrix / mod_targets in the snapshot). source: lfo1|lfo2|env1|env2 (the mod envelopes)|midiVelocity|midiNote|mpePressure|mpeTimbre|cc<n> (cc1 mod wheel, cc11 expression, cc74 cutoff). target: a VOICE param id (filterFreq, filterResonance, level1..4, fineTune1..4, pan1..4, pulseWidth1..4, lfoDepth1..2, lfoRate1..2, ampAttack, filterAttack, modAttack1..2, ...) - never masterLevel or the FX. depth: the modulation as a fraction of the target's range, ADDED to the knob (+0.3 = up to 30 % above it; negative pulls down). clear:true removes the route. A knob's own value is instrument.set_param, not this

commands.name: Set Sampler Param
commands.args: { track, param, value, note? } - note = a DRUM PAD's own Simpler on that track (the kit is promoted to per-pad Simplers on first use), so every sampler param is per-pad: "tighten the kick's decay" = sampler.set {track, note:36, param:"decay_ms", value:120}

commands.name: Sampler Editor
commands.args: { track? (default: the selected track), note? (a drum pad: opens that pad's Simpler, promoting the kit on first use) }

commands.name: Drum Rack
commands.args: { track? (default: the selected track) } - toggle the kit's Drum Rack editor

commands.name: Match Clip to Key
commands.args: { track, clip | scene } - scene matches a Loop Deck slot clip to the song key

commands.name: Follow Song Key
commands.args: { track, clip, on?: bool (absent = toggle), root_note?: 0-11 or a tonic name ("C", "F#", "Bb") } â FOLLOW THE SONG KEY: the clip re-pitches itself whenever the key track changes, by the nearest interval from its own key to the song's. root_note is what key the CLIP is in and is required the first time (without it the engine has nothing to move it from and the switch does nothing). Composes with a fixed clip.pitch rather than replacing it. Read tracks[].clips[].follows_key + root_note. Use clip.match_key instead for a ONE-OFF re-pitch that then stays put

commands.name: Stretch Quality
commands.args: { track, clip, mode } â which algorithm warps and pitches this clip. mode is "Off", one of the engine's own names (read tracks[].clips[].stretch_mode; this build ships SoundTouch Normal + Better), or the aliases "normal" / "better" / "default". Better costs more CPU and keeps transients cleaner; Normal is the cheap one. An unknown name is refused NAMING what is available

commands.args: the LIVE arpeggiator MIDI FX device on the track (non-destructive - the clip's notes stay put; to bake an arpeggio INTO a clip's notes use midi.arpeggiate, and for swing/groove feel use clip.set_groove or midi.quantize, never this) { track, on?:bool=true, style?:"up"|"down"|"updown"|"downup"|"updown_inc"|"converge"|"diverge"|"pinky_up"|"thumb_up"|"played"|"chord"|"random", rate_beats?:double (1/16 = 0.25) or rate?:"1/16"|"1/8D"|"1/4T" (the snapshot's own spelling â echo it back verbatim) + rate_modifier?:"straight"|"dotted"|"triplet", octaves?:1-8, gate?:0.05-1, swing?:0.5-0.75 (0.5 straight; swings the PATTERN THE ARP GENERATES - to swing a clip's own existing notes use clip.set_groove or midi.quantize), repeats?:1-8, chance?:0-1, vel_decay?:-1..1, shift?:-24..24 semitones, scale?:"off"|"major"|"minor"|"dorian"|"phrygian"|"lydian"|"mixolydian"|"harmonic_minor"|"pentatonic_major"|"pentatonic_minor"|"blues"|"whole_tone", key?:0-11 or a note name ("D#" â the snapshot's spelling), hold?:bool, retrigger?:"off"|"note"|"bar", bypassed?:bool (keeps the device + its settings, passes notes through â `on:false` DELETES it) }

commands.args: { rack, chain, name?, volume_db?, pan?: -1..1, mute?, solo? }

commands.args: { track, devices:[ eq | comp#1 | plugin:0 | <plug-in name> â¦ ], name? }

commands.name: Crop Sample
commands.args: { track, note? } - crops the sample to its START/END region: the region is written as a new wav in the project and loaded in its place (START/END reset to the whole file; undo restores the old file)

commands.name: Add Sample Layer
commands.args: { track, path, lo_note?:0-127 (default 0), hi_note?:0-127 (default 127), lo_vel?:1-127 (default 1), hi_vel?:1-127 (default 127), root_note?:0-127 (default = lo_note, or 60 for the whole keyboard), gain_db?:-24..12, key_fade?:0-24, vel_fade?:0-64, note? (a drum pad's Simpler) } - a multi-sample zone: this file plays instead of the main sample for keys lo..hi at velocities lo_vel..hi_vel; EVERY zone holding the note plays, and key_fade / vel_fade ramp a zone in and out over that many keys / velocity steps at each end, so two zones overlapping by their fade widths CROSSFADE (their gains sum to one). Slice mode ignores layers. Up to 16; returns the layer's index; the snapshot lists them under sampler.layers. On a drum track, note picks the pad: velocity layers per pad

commands.name: Set Sample Layer
commands.args: { track, index, lo_note?, hi_note?, lo_vel?, hi_vel?, root_note?, gain_db?, key_fade?, vel_fade?, note? }

commands.args: { on?: bool (omit = toggle), octave?: -2..2 (the A key = MIDI 60 at 0), velocity?: 1-127 } - the computer MIDI keyboard (âK): a s d f g h j k l ; ' play the white keys from C on the focused instrument track, w e t y u o p the black keys, Z/X shift the octave, C/V the velocity

commands.name: Master Safety Limiter
commands.args: { on?: bool (omit = toggle) } - the master SAFETY limiter: a ceiling-only -1 dBTP limiter (no loudness makeup) on the master chain; new projects seed one

commands.name: Gate Towers/Tape View
commands.args: { tape?: bool (omit = toggle) } - the gate face's hero picture: TOWERS (detect + attenuation meters with the rhythm and key ribbons) or the TAPE (six seconds of the detector, lit where the gate is open)

commands.name: Multiband Field/Tapes View
commands.args: { tapes?: bool (omit = toggle) } - the multiband compressor face's hero picture: the FIELD (the spectrum in and out, the gap between them the reduction, with the band towers) or the TAPES (six seconds of each band's level with its threshold and reduction)

commands.name: Saturation Field/Cards View
commands.args: { cards?: bool (omit = toggle) } - the multiband saturation face's hero picture: the HEAT FIELD (the spectrum in and out with each band's generated harmonics drawn where they land, the knee lines, the heat towers) or the WAVESHAPER CARDS (a card per band: the curve, the live harmonic stack, THD and heat)

commands.name: OTT Field/Tapes View
commands.args: { tapes?: bool (omit = toggle) } - the OTT face's hero picture: the FIELD (the spectrum in and out, the gap between them the levelling - red pulled down, warm lifted - with the bipolar towers) or the TAPES (six seconds of each band's level in and out around the -30 dB target every band is pulled toward)

commands.name: Clipper Tape/Scope View
commands.args: { scope?: bool (omit = toggle) } - the clipper face's hero picture: the TAPE (six seconds of the master with the loudness band under the peaks, everything the input reaches above the ceiling filled red - the shave - with the IN / OUT crest bars and the headroom won) or the SCOPE (the wave at sample scale with the top coming off, the corner shaped by hardness)

commands.name: Overdrive Field/Scope View
commands.args: { scope?: bool (omit = toggle) } - the overdrive face's hero picture: the FIELD (the spectrum in and out - the grit the drive adds filled warm above the input, what the band-pass took away red below it - with the focus curtain and the tone tilt as gain curves on the 0 dB line) or the SCOPE (the wave bending into the ceiling at -DRIVE dBFS, the squash filled between the ghost and the driven output)

commands.name: Saturation Scope/Tape View
commands.args: { tape?: bool (omit = toggle) } - the single-band saturation face's hero picture: the SCOPE (the wave through the curve at its live level - the input as a ghost, the shaped output bright, the knee as dashed lines pinned at 55 % of the lane so the clip is the picture) or the HEAT TAPE (six seconds of the input and shaped-output peaks against the knee horizon the output flattens against, the input above the knee filled warm to red, a THD lane under it)

commands.name: Delay Scope/Tape View
commands.args: { tape?: bool (omit = toggle) } - the delay face's hero picture: the ECHO SCOPE (the repeats this setting makes - bars at the delay time falling by the feedback, amber where the loop's tone has darkened them, over the note values of one bar at the session tempo, with the miss to the nearest note) or the ECHO TAPE (six seconds of the dry hits and every echo they threw, against the beat grid scrolling with the transport)

commands.name: Reverb Scope/Tape View
commands.args: { tape?: bool (omit = toggle) } - the reverb face's hero picture: the TAIL SCOPE (the reverb's own shape on a log-time axis - the pre-delay gap, the comb onsets, the fall to -60 dB at the decay time, with every hit sliding down the curve as a pip) or the RING TAPE (six seconds of the dry and the wet on one axis with the WASH filled amber wherever the reverb is louder than the source, and the pre-delay bracket + decay slope laid on the newest hit)

commands.name: IR Reverb Field/Print View
commands.args: { print?: bool (omit = toggle) } - the IR reverb face's hero picture: the TAIL WATERFALL (the impulse as a spectrogram - time across, frequency up, brightness is level - with the tone cutoff as the dashed ceiling, the true RT60 as the amber line and the pre-delay as the black column at the left) or the ROOM PRINT (the first 100 ms of the impulse at full zoom, where room / hall / plate actually differ, beside the whole tail falling to -60 dB)

commands.name: Width Stage/Field View
commands.args: { field?: bool (omit = toggle) } - the stereo width face's picture: the STAGE (a top-down listening position - every sample of the master a point in a fan in front of the listener, mono a bright column straight ahead, wide out to the two speaker marks at +-30 degrees, anti-phase past the red rays; the input as a ghost fan, twelve seconds of correlation along the floor) or the FIELD (width per frequency - each band's Side-against-Mid opening as a column mirrored about the centre line, the input a dim ghost, the output lit, red where a band crosses into anti-phase)

commands.name: Spectrogram View
commands.args: { picture?: "tape"|"ridge", under?: "off"|"bands"|"notes", full?: bool } - the analyzer face's three switches, any subset in one call (a bare call cycles the picture). PICTURE is the waterfall's geometry: the TAPE (flat and measurable - a bar:beat ruler along the top, a piano note ruler down the frequency axis with the C octaves ruled through the field, the loudest partial of every column traced as one white thread so a melody reads as a line, and a hover readout of frequency / note / cents / dB / bar) or the RIDGE (the last twelve seconds in perspective, the newest spectrum the lit ridge at the front and older columns receding into the dark). UNDER is the drawer beneath the picture: "off", "bands" (the eight band histories - sub / bass / lo mid / mid / hi mid / pres / bril / air - plus momentary LUFS over the last minute, with per-lane mean and max: exactly the rows track.spectrogram hands you, so the user is watching your own numbers) or "notes" (a twelve-lane chroma tape of which pitch classes have been sounding, with the detected key and its confidence). FULL drops the glass rail and lays the peak / LUFS / tilt readouts over the picture as a HUD - the biggest picture per pixel
